- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in the early part of the forecast horizon (first 5–10 days).
- After a sharp price spike, model tends to overshoot and then overcorrect, creating a “peak then dip” pattern that doesn’t match true market behavior.
- Model exhibits strong mean reversion bias — it overreacts to recent volatility and fails to capture sustained trends.
- Forecast horizon 30d shows persistent underestimation of late-period price declines, particularly after mid-forecast.
- Model fails to account for seasonal or event-driven corrections — e.g., after high prices, it doesn’t adjust downward as quickly as actual market data.
- Model is overly sensitive to recent high values, leading to “recency bias” — it assumes recent trends will continue, even when they reverse.
- Model underestimates the impact of policy or supply shocks in the final 5–10 days of the forecast.
- Model tends to smooth out volatility, underestimating short-term price swings and overestimating long-term stability.
